data.name: Gnesh
data.gender_notes: Gnesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Ganesh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'ganana' meaning 'to count', and 'ishta' meaning 'dear to'. Lord Ganesha is known as the remover of obstacles, and the god of wisdom and good fortune. He is revered and loved by millions of Hindus all over the world. The name Gnesh carries the meaning “Lord Ganesha” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi. Parents who choose Gnesh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord ganesha and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ganesh represents wisdom, knowledge, and the power of the mind over matter. He is the remover of obstacles and the patron of arts and sciences. He is also known as the god of beginnings, and is invoked at the start of any new venture or endeavor.
data.etymology: Gnesh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Ganesha.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gnesh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Lord Ganesh is a widely revered deity in Hindu culture and is often worshipped before starting any new venture or endeavor. He is also the patron god of arts, literature, and learning. The popular mythology around Ganesh includes his story of hanging his head in penance when his parents were insulted, and the subsequent removal of his head to appease the gods, only for his head to be replaced by the lovely elephant head. Cultural traditions include creating and worshipping beautiful statues and icons of Ganesh, with the most popular being the annual Ganesh Chaturthi festival where people immerse and allow the statues to disintegrate in water, symbolizing the cycle of birth, life, death, and rebirth.
data.spiritual_significance: Lord Ganesh is regarded as the remover of obstacles, and is believed to bestow wisdom, good fortune, and success in all endeavors. He is often invoked during religious and spiritual rituals as he is considered to be the gatekeeper of the divine. He represents the qualities of large-heartedness, generosity, wisdom, and an insatiable thirst for knowledge. The spiritual significance of the name Ganesh is deeply rooted in the philosophy of Hinduism, which teaches that the removal of internal obstacles, such as egoism and selfishness, is necessary to attain enlightenment and inner peace. Lord Ganesh serves as a reminder of this fundamental truth, and inspires us to strive for spiritual growth and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ganesh symbolizes the power of wisdom and new beginnings. His elephant head represents the removal of obstacles and the ability to carry heavy responsibilities. He is revered as the god of wisdom and the deity who brings good fortune.
